answer: Each identity books a depot slot and delivers one cedar crate holding a prism standard flashing a pulse pattern, locking a 65-credit bond. The depot scans the standard, matches its spectrum and pulse pattern to the manifest, and burns the serial, so no crate counts twice. Slots are tiered: the first costs 34, the kth costs 34+5(k-1), the 1000th costs 5029, and 1000 fake identities pay 2,531,500 plus 65,000 locked. A rented-crate ring fails because the serial is already burned and a second scan mismatches the manifest. An honest operator pays 34 once and reclaims the bond after a clean scan.
